1.title: Chapter Test: Introduction
1.description: Final task of chapter 1. Checks: iostream, compilation, cout.

practice.description:
Write a program with `#include <iostream>`, `int main()`, output three lines via `std::cout`:
```
C++
Lesson 1
Done
```
Finish with `return 0;`.

2.title: Chapter Test: Fundamentals
2.description: Final task of chapter 2. Checks: types, cin/cout, references.

practice.description:
Read two integers via `std::cin`, output via `std::cout`:
```
Sum: 15
Product: 50
```

**stdin:**
```
5
10
```

3.title: Chapter Test: Control Flow
3.description: Final task of chapter 3. Checks: if, for, break.

practice.description:
Via `for` from 1 to 10 output only odds:
```
1
3
5
7
9
```

4.title: Chapter Test: Functions
4.description: Final task of chapter 4. Checks: functions, overloading, references.

practice.description:
Create:
- `int square(int x)` — returns `x * x`
- `void incr(int &x)` — increments `x` by 1 via reference

In `main`:
- `n = 5`, output `square(5)`
- output `incr(n)` (n becomes 6)

```
25
6
```

5.title: Chapter Test: Arrays and Strings
5.description: Final task of chapter 5. Checks: vector, string, range-for.

practice.description:
Given `std::vector<int> nums = {3, 7, 2, 9, 5};`.

Output:
```
Sum: 26
Max: 9
String: hello (5)
```

Last one — `std::string s = "hello";` and `s.size()`.

6.title: Chapter Test: Classes
6.description: Final task of chapter 6. Checks: class, constructor, private, static.

practice.description:
Class `Book`:
- `private std::string title`, `private int pages`
- constructor `Book(std::string t, int p)`
- getters `getTitle()`, `getPages()`

In `main` create `Book b("Java", 500)` and output:
```
Java: 500
```

7.title: Chapter Test: OOP
7.description: Final task of chapter 7. Checks: inheritance, virtual functions.

practice.description:
Abstract class `Shape` with `virtual double area() = 0` and `virtual std::string name() = 0`.

Subclasses:
- `Rectangle` — `width * height`, name `"Rectangle"`
- `Circle` — `3.14 * r * r`, name `"Circle"`

Via `std::vector<Shape*>` or `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Shape>>` output:
```
Rectangle: 6
Circle: 12.56
```

8.title: Chapter Test: STL Containers
8.description: Final task of chapter 8. Checks: vector, map, set.

practice.description:
1. `std::vector<int> v = {1, 2, 3};` — output `size`.
2. `std::map<std::string, int> m; m["a"] = 1; m["b"] = 2;` — output `m["a"]`.
3. `std::set<int> s = {1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3};` — output `size`.

```
Vector: 3
Map a: 1
Set: 3
```

9.title: Chapter Test: Algorithms
9.description: Final task of chapter 9. Checks: sort, accumulate, lambdas.

practice.description:
Given `std::vector<int> v = {5, 3, 8, 2, 7};`.

1. `std::sort` — output sorted (space-separated).
2. `std::accumulate` — output sum.
3. Lambda filter: output all > 4 via `for_each` and lambda.

```
Sorted: 2 3 5 7 8
Sum: 25
> 4: 5 7 8
```

10.title: Chapter Test: Smart Pointers
10.description: Final task of chapter 10. Checks: unique_ptr, shared_ptr.

practice.description:
1. `std::unique_ptr<int> p = std::make_unique<int>(42);` — output `*p`.
2. `std::shared_ptr<int> q = std::make_shared<int>(10);` — output `*q` and `q.use_count()`.

```
unique: 42
shared: 10 (count 1)
```

11.title: Chapter Test: Exceptions
11.description: Final task of chapter 11. Checks: throw, try/catch, custom exceptions.

practice.description:
1. Create `class MyError : public std::runtime_error { using std::runtime_error::runtime_error; };`.
2. Function `check(int x)`: if `x < 0` — `throw MyError("negative")`.
3. In `main`: call `check(-1)` in `try/catch` and output `Error: negative`.

```
Error: negative
```

12.title: Chapter Test: Templates
12.description: Final task of chapter 12. Checks: function templates, class templates.

practice.description:
1. `template <typename T> T maxOf(T a, T b) { return a > b ? a : b; }`.
2. Output `maxOf(3, 7)` and `maxOf(3.5, 2.1)`.

```
7
3.5
```

13.title: Chapter Test: Final
13.description: Final task of the course. Checks: classes, STL, algorithms.

practice.description:
Class `Product` with `std::string name`, `double price`, getters.

`std::vector<Product> products = { {"A", 100}, {"B", 200}, {"C", 50} };`

1. Sum via `std::accumulate` with a lambda.
2. First with price > 150 via `std::find_if`.

```
Sum: 350
Expensive: B
```
